title: Atlas Core Hotel PMS sandbox security assessment
scope: Persistent local-only Hotel PMS sandbox provider, operator execution controls, tenant isolation, idempotency, provider state, and rollback

approved_targets: Persistent synthetic Hotel PMS SQLite databases under disposable test and local runtime paths
Loopback Atlas Operator and Gateway services
prohibited_actions: Contact a live PMS or hotel account
Accept or store a provider credential
Represent sandbox state as a real reservation outcome

assets: Provider-side cancellation review and inventory state
trust_boundaries: Browser mutation to localhost operator token and tenant binding
Approved Atlas proposal to fixed sandbox executor
Atlas execution request to separate persistent sandbox database
Provider state and bounded receipt back to operator
data_flows: Synthetic reservation versions into Company Memory and Cartographer
Human-approved cancellation proposal into the execution outbox
Exact confirmation phrase and stable idempotency key into the sandbox
Inventory release or rollback into tenant-scoped sandbox state

threats.name: Operator route invokes an arbitrary or live executor
threats.control: Operator queue route fixes the executor to hotel-pms-sandbox and run or rollback routes reject receipts owned by any other executor

threats.name: Cross-tenant reservation access
threats.control: Mutation token binds the body and header tenant; provider reads and writes use tenant_id plus reservation_id keys

threats.name: Duplicate inventory release
threats.control: Provider persists unique idempotency and execution identifiers and returns the original reference on replay across process restarts

threats.name: Proposal payload targets a different reservation
threats.control: Provider requires the payload reservation identifier to equal the immutable proposal entity identifier

threats.name: UI implies a real PMS action
threats.control: Workspace, confirmation dialog, capability name, provider identifier, and receipt reference all explicitly identify the local sandbox

threats.name: Rollback silently invents prior state
threats.control: Provider stores previous review and inventory states with the original action and requires that receipt for rollback

findings.finding: The adapter deliberately has no network endpoint, credential field, or live-provider mode.
A live hotel adapter remains a separate security boundary requiring vendor sandbox certification, credential custody, provider-native idempotency, rate-limit handling, and incident procedures.
The sandbox reservation view exposes synthetic reservation identifiers and state to any local process able to access the loopback operator; it must not be used for real guest data.

validation: Ninety-one Python 3.12 tests passed, including provider restart idempotency, tenant isolation, exact confirmations, full operator execution, rollback, and denial of non-sandbox executors
Fresh core, SDK, Gateway, and Operator wheels installed with no broken requirements
Installed remote SDK and Gateway completed a sandbox cancellation and verified provider inventory released
Live browser completed seed, approval, queue, execution, and rollback with exact typed confirmations
Live browser showed released inventory after execution and restored held inventory after rollback with no console errors or desktop horizontal overflow
residual_risk: The sandbox is implementation evidence, not a vendor-certified PMS integration.
No real guest data, provider credentials, network calls, or external actions were used.
A live adapter requires a new focused security assessment and explicit authorization.
This assessment is not a compliance certification.
